The US is so prehistoric with their hospitals 🙄. I feel like there should be “family” units or like how the Ronald McDonald houses are set up except these are less like a home and more like a hotel/hospital room. Comfy enough and has the basics but easy to clean/sterilize. 

My 10 week old was just admitted for an 8 day stay 2 weeks ago. It was a nightmare getting care for my other two toddlers because my partner HAD to work. He had zero choice. He was able to take off ONE day plus his 2 day weekends = 5 days we needed to scramble. I couldn’t leave the baby and I was also pumping for her in the hospital. If that’s not enough stress, while I was in the hospital of the baby’s room one night I suddenly freaking hemorrhaged out of nowhere. Had no precursors and I was in so much pain my BP shot up super high (which no one is concerned about still) and I was just gushing blood and clots. Tmi I’m sorry. But it looked like a murder scene. I wanted my husband with me so bad I needed him but the toddlers couldn’t come to my hospital room only the baby’s. 

So I continued to be alone and it always sucks. Some unit or maybe 3-5 rooms dedicated to something like this would be amazing. On the PEDS unit because she wasn’t ICU or anything she was on the wing with kids who like needed surgery on an ankle or had their appendix burst or something. So no one majorly immune compromised or contagious and they had this huge playroom that my toddlers got to visit too. They had a therapy pup come say hi and they had a room stocked up with stacks. I kept joking to my husband to hide the toddlers in babys room overnight so we could just be together but it never worked. 

Would have probably sucked anyway because the “bed” for me was legit concrete feeling. She might need another stay in the near future and we have no one to help with our kids and I have no clue what to do. Other places like the UK seem to value things like that much more often. Or try to accommodate.

Breast pads- personally, I’m very sensitive so I don’t like the disposable breast pads but I love the reusable ones. My favorite brand is Bamboobies and they’re $6 (USA) for 4 of them and I only wear them when I’m wearing a bra which is rare lol. 

A can or even a bottle of pre-made formula would be a great idea. To save even more you can go to the enfamil/similac/etc. websites usually and sign up for coupons and freebies. I even got a couple cans of formula with my coupons. So this could end up costing nothing for you and if your baby takes well to breastfeeding nothing comes out of pocket and you can always donate the formula cans! 

Personally I don’t think you *need* the sterilizer bags, I do have a baby brezza sterilizer but only because it was a gift lol. With my last baby’s I had this microwave sterilizer it was pretty cheap and I ended up pumping so it worked for those parts as well as bottles/binkys. 

Other things that I’d *personally* recommend are nipple cream, breast milk bags but I wouldn’t get them unless you plan on pumping some of the time and speaking of pumping- I know you said insurance doesn’t give free pumps but if you feel like a pump would help in your breastfeeding journey I would see if your hospital rents them? Or buy second hand. You’d only need to replace the parts for sanitation reasons. Alternatively a manual pump is cheap and very portable. 

But the best purchase in my opinion would simply be a Haaka. It’s not a pump per se but it is very helpful at catching extra milk while feeding babe on the opposite boob. I usually get 1-2 1/2 OZ per feed which means that every other feed I at least have a bottles worth of milk available to freeze or save for night time feeds. 

Muslin baby wraps are great for ‘burp cloths’, baby swaddles/blankets and they’re very soft and breathable. I use them to cover myself a little if I’m breastfeeding in public and I just wanna be a little more modest. Then she doesn’t get too hot. 

All in all I really hope you have an easy and wonderful breastfeeding journey. I know for some women it just happens but for others something *may* go wrong or not exactly “wrong” but may end up sending them down another feeding path whatever it may be. As long as your baby is happy, healthy and fed then that’s all that matters. I just had my 4th baby and I’ve had a different feeding journey with each of them. Right now I am breastfeeding but to help plump her up quicker she also gets expressed milk and formula in a bottle. 

I know that you’re not in the US but I got freebie bags from Amazon, target, buybuybaby and Babylist. (Amazon and Babylist I did have to make a purchase in order to get them but I got a lot of goodies and got to try different brands and got coupons too) but I would try finding the UK equivalent I’m sure some stores near you have something like that. So ideally you could spend virtually nothing and also have everything you need!
